parts: I’ll read the continuation note and the project’s established results, then clarify the polynomial picture and compare the proposed induction with your truncation idea.

The note leaves the induction open. Its concrete starting idea is to bound recurrence coefficients, then use their product to control a finite approximation to \(H_\lambda\). Your proposal adds another step: proving a zero statement that survives as the approximation covers larger heights. I’m checking how those two steps could fit together.

The existing bounds already support the approximation side of your idea: increasing the degree lets us control larger real-height windows. The part still to find is an induction that controls zeros. Real roots of \(P_N(u)\) do not imply real zeros of the finite Fourier approximation; even Gaussian quadrature gives a simple example of that distinction.

A useful distinction is emerging: an induction could carry coefficient bounds, a controlled replacement for the omitted tail, or a certificate about zeros in a growing region. I’ll spell out what each would need to carry from one degree to the next, and save the discussion as an exploratory note so we can continue from it.
